notes.text: I saw — In a vision. The Lord - The Divine Majesty as he subsisteth in three persons. His train - His royal and judicial robe; for he is represented as a judge.

Stood — As ministers attending upon their Lord. Seraphim - An order of holy angels, thus called from fire and burning, which this word properly signifies; to represent either their nature, which is bright and glorious, subtile, and pure; or their property, of fervent zeal for God's service and glory. Covered - Out of profound reverence.

Cried — Singing in consort. Holy - This is repeated thrice, to intimate the Trinity of persons united in the Divine essence. Glory - Of the effects and demonstrations of his glorious holiness, as well as of his power, wisdom, and goodness.
The posts — Together with the door itself. Such violent motions were commonly tokens of God's anger. Smoak - Which elsewhere is a token of God's presence and acceptance, but here of his anger.

l am — I am a great sinner, as many other ways, so particularly by my lips. I am an unclean branch of an unclean tree; besides my own uncleanness, I have both by my omissions and commissions involved myself in the guilt of their sins. Have seen - The sight of this glorious and holy God gives me cause to fear that he is come to judgment against me.
Flew — By God's command. A coal - Both a token and an instrument of purification. The altar - Of burnt-offering.
Laid it — So as only to touch my lips, and not to burn them; which God could easily effect. Lo - This is a sign that I have pardoned and purged the uncleanness of thy lips.

Who — To deliver the following message. The change of the number, I and us, is very remarkable; and both being meant of one and the same Lord, do sufficiently intimate a plurality of persons in the Godhead.

glossa.text:
*In the year,* etc. ((HIER.)) Ozias himself is Azarias, etc., *as far as* falling upon his face, he cries out with a loud voice to the Lord.

 *King Ozias.* The king, namely the leper, who usurped the priesthood.

*I saw the Lord.* Christ, namely. The Son was seen in the habit of one reigning; the Holy Spirit spoke, because of the fellowship of majesty and the unity of substance.

*Upon a throne high,* etc. ((HIER.)) He who sees the Lord reigning in the heavenly powers sees him upon a throne high and lifted up, which are the Thrones and the Dominations, etc.

Some say that the seraphim are powers in heaven attending upon God and praising him, which are sent upon ministries chiefly to those who have need of purgation, and, for certain sins, in part to punishments.

((ID.)) Cherubim, a multitude of knowledge, upon whom the Lord is shown to sit after the manner of a charioteer, whence: *Thou that sittest upon the cherubim,* etc. But the seraphim, apart from this place, I do not remember to have read in the canonical Scriptures. They err therefore who are wont to write in their prayers: Thou that sittest upon the cherubim and seraphim.

*They stood.* ((ID.)) That is, they stand attending upon God; they fly, showing forth God; they lay bare as it were the middle part; they do not make manifest the things that are veiled; they do not veil the things that are known.

*Six wings to one.* ((ID.)) Victorinus understands the twelve apostles. But we, the twelve stones of the altar which iron did not touch, and the twelve gems in the diadem of the priest.

((ID.)) The angels are said to have wings, because they dwell in the higher places, or because of their swift running to and fro in all things, as the winds also are called winged.

*With two they veiled his face.* What things were before these I know not, etc., *as far as* the angels also and the preachers teach nothing thereof; likewise:

*They veiled the feet.* ((HIER.)) What is to be after this world we know not: the middle things, however, which were made in six days or ages, or are made; we know only *With two they veiled,* because we have knowledge of the present alone.

((ID.)) My Hebrew has entered by a far other way, etc., *as far as* and then, being truly purged in the lips, I said to the Lord: *Behold I, send me.*

*And they cried.* ((ID.)) They do not say it lightly, but pronounce with a cry a confession salutary for all: Holy, holy, holy, because they themselves also, namely the seraphim, are holy: for nothing is holier than these: but they marvel that the Son so humbled himself and underwent the cross, and became known to earthly things.

*Holy, holy,* etc. The mystery of the Trinity. In both Testaments the Trinity is preached, the Lord Christ, namely, who here is of four letters, which is set down properly of God: Iod, He, Iod, He; that is, two *ia,* which doubled make the ineffable name of God.

*The whole earth is full.* ((ID.)) And it shall be filled, etc., *as far as* after two and forty years from the passion of the Lord.
*The lintels.* In the Old Testament the Lord spoke, etc., *as far as* which taking up we say: *We know in part, and we prophesy in part ((I Cor. XIII))*.

*Polluted.* ((ID.)) This he says because of the fellowship of the people, with whom he was constrained to speak. It is harmful to live with sinners.

*I dwell.* Note that one must not tarry with sinners.

*And I have seen with my eyes the King, the Lord of hosts: and one flew to me.* So Abraham, after he had seen the Lord and heard his voice, confesses himself to be ashes and dust, because however great the dignity of men may be, it grows cheap in comparison of him.

*Of the seraphim.* ((ID.)) Seraphim with *m* we say in the masculine gender, with *n* in the neuter gender plural. Seraphim, however, can be said in the singular, as cherubim and cherub.

*And in his hand.* That is, by his working, that is, of Christ. The coal, that is, charity, which with the tongs, that is, the teaching of the two Testaments, he had taken from the altar, and had set before Isaias for an example.

*A coal.* ((ID.)) The Seventy: a carbuncle, a fiery stone, which because of its flame-like colour is called igneous.

*With tongs.* ((ID.)) This is the ladder of Jacob, the sword twice sharpened, etc., *as far as* comprehending the word of God with the double edge of the precepts.

*From the altar.* Which John saw in the Apocalypse, which is full of fiery coals, wherewith sins can be purged.

*Behold I have touched thy lips:* whence: *What may be given to thee, or what may be added to thee for a deceitful tongue? The sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals that lay waste ((Psal. CXIX))*. This is the word of God, of which it is said: Thou hast coals of fire, thou shalt sit upon them, these shall be to thee for a help.

*And the iniquity shall be taken away.* ((ID.)) Jeremias, who was a boy, and therefore almost free from sin, is purged by the touch of a hand alone. But to Isaias, who says: I am a man polluted in the lips, an angel is sent with a coal.

*Whom shall I send?* He does not compel, but seeks the will: for the will alone deserves the reward. But Isaias, as one purged, offers himself of his own accord.

*Send me.* ((ID.)) He thinks that he is to announce good, etc., *as far as* that it was not of rashness but of obedience that he offered himself.

notes.text: Ye — Ye potentates and rulers of the earth. Glory - By an humble and thankful acknowledgment of it.
Give, &c. — The honour which he deserves: own him as the Almighty, and the only true God. Holiness - Or, in his holy and beautiful house.

The waters — Above in the clouds, which are called waters, Gen. i, 7 chap. xviii, 11. The Divine power displays itself in those high places, which are far above the reach of all earthly potentates. Many - Upon the clouds, in which there are vast treasures of water, and upon which God is said to sit or ride, chap. xviii, 10, 11; civ, 3.
Lebanon — A place famous for strong and lofty cedars.

Them — The cedars; which being broken by the thunder, the parts of them are suddenly and violently hurled hither and thither. Sirion - An high mountain beyond Jordan joining to Lebanon. Lebanon and Sirion are said to skip or leap, both here, and chap. cxiv, 4, by a poetical hyperbole.
The flames — The lightnings.
Kadesh — An eminent wilderness, vast and terrible, and well known to the Israelites, and wherein possibly they had seen, and observed some such effects of thunder.

To calve — Through the terror it causes, which hastens the birth. He names the hinds, because they bring forth their young with difficulty, Job xxxix, 1, 2. Discovereth - Hebrew. maketh bare, of its trees, which it breaks or strips of their leaves. Glory - Having shewed the terrible effects of God's power in other places, he now shews the blessed privilege of God's people, that are praising God in his temple, when the rest of the world are trembling under the tokens of his displeasure.

The flood — The most violent waters, which sometimes fall from the clouds upon the earth. These are fitly mentioned, as being many times the companions of great thunders. And this may be alleged as another reason, why God's people praised him in his temple, because as he sends terrible tempests and thunders, so he also restrains and over-rules them. Sitteth - He doth sit, and will sit as king forever, sending such tempests when it pleaseth him. He praises God for delivering him, and exhorts others to praise him, ver. 1-5. Recollects his former security, and his prayer when in trouble, ver. 6-10. And stirs himself up to thankfulness, ver. 11, 12. A Psalm and song, at the dedication of the house of David. Title of the psalm. Song - A psalm to be sung with the voice to an instrument. David - At the dedication of David's house, which was built, 2 Sam. v, 11, and doubtless was dedicated, as God had commanded.

glossa.text:
*A psalm of David in the consummation.* ((ID.)) The ark brought back from the Philistines, etc., *as far as* that they may offer themselves to such a consummator.

*Bring to the Lord.* ((ID.)) First he admonishes that sacrifices be offered.

 *The sons of rams.* ((AUG.)) Because assault is not wanting, etc., *as far as* and the seventy-two disciples sent to preach are signified.

*The voice of the Lord.* ((CASS.)) The preaching of Christ terrified minds within, which is, that it gave the spirit of fear to the Jews and to the Gentiles.

((GREG.)) This man ascends from the lowest, that is, from the spirit of fear to the spirit of wisdom, etc., *as far as* that is, spiritual understanding: these the Lord shakes.

((HIER.)) As a husbandman a barren land, etc., *as far as* and he will give strength, and will bless the same in eternal peace.

*The voice of the Lord upon the waters,* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the establishing of the Church, where he enumerates the powers of the Holy Ghost with great proclamation.

*Of Libanus.* Libanus is interpreted a whitening. *The cedars of Libanus,* that is, high men lifted up in earthly things, whom God by breaking will crush small, that is, will bring them back from pride to himself through his beloved Son: and this he will crush by the spirit of fortitude, as a unicorn taken is crushed.
*The desert.* ((CASS., AUG.)) The Jewish people, etc., *as far as* whence flows the living water.

*The Lord.* He shews what is done for the Church now established.

*I have given,* he says, *you power to tread down upon serpents.* But as it is unheard of that stags should strike every kind of wild beast with the horn; so that the Apostles, unlettered, should refute all philosophy.

 *A flood.* ((CASS.)) The waters of baptism, which purges the crimes of the world.

notes.text: We are not debtors to the flesh — We ought not to follow it.

The deeds of the flesh — Not only evil actions, but evil desires, tempers, thoughts. If ye mortify - Kill, destroy these. Ye shall live - The life of faith more abundantly here, and hereafter the life of glory.

For as many as are led by the Spirit of God — In all the ways of righteousness. They are the sons of God - Here St. Paul enters upon the description of those blessings which he comprises, ver. 30, in the word glorified; though, indeed, he does not describe mere glory, but that which is still mingled with the cross. The sum is, through sufferings to glory.

For ye — Who are real Christians. Have not received the spirit of bondage - The Holy Ghost was not properly a spirit of bondage, even in the time of the Old Testament. Yet there was something of bondage remaining even in those who then had received the Spirit. Again - As the Jews did before. We - All and every believer. Cry - The word denotes a vehement speaking, with desire, confidence, constancy. Abba, Father - The latter word explains the former. By using both the Syriac and the Greek word, St. Paul seems to point out the joint cry both of the Jewish and gentile believers. The spirit of bondage here seems directly to mean, those operations of the Holy Spirit by which the soul, on its first conviction, feels itself in bondage to sin, to the world, to Satan, and obnoxious to the wrath of God. This, therefore, and the Spirit of adoption, are one and the same Spirit, only manifesting itself in various operations, according to the various circumstances of the persons.

The same Spirit beareth witness with our spirit — With the spirit of every true believer, by a testimony distinct from that of his own spirit, or the testimony of a good conscience. Happy they who enjoy this clear and constant.

Joint heirs — That we may know it is a great inheritance which God will give us for he hath given a great one to his Son. If we suffer with him - Willingly and cheerfully, for righteousness' sake. This is a new proposition, referring to what follows.

glossa.text: *But if by the Spirit.* Either by the Holy Spirit or by our own: which nevertheless is not so, save by the working of the Holy Spirit.

*They are driven.* He says they are driven, not they are ruled. For it is more to be driven than to be ruled: for we say that one is driven, as scarcely doing anything; but that he is ruled, as already doing something, who is therefore ruled that he may act rightly. But they are driven, not because they do nothing of themselves, but because, that they may do something, they are impelled by the force of grace.

((AUG., lib. de Correp. et Grat., c. 2.)) Let them not therefore deceive themselves who say: To what end for us, etc., *as far as* let them rejoice that they have received.

*For you have not received,* etc. You ought to be sons, not servants, because you have not received the spirit of bondage: which makes men serve unwilling through fear of punishment.

*But you have received the spirit of adoption.* It is the same spirit, but because of diverse works it is differently named: he is called the spirit of wrath to the Egyptians, to whom the water divided by the spirit did harm. The son of Israel is not called [a spirit] of wrath, to whom the divided water was of profit. He is the spirit of fear to those who, convicted by the law of their sins and of their own weakness, did not understand the grace of the spirit. He is the spirit of liberty by his working to those to whom regeneration unto life eternal, and faith which works through love, has been imparted. One spirit therefore, which makes two fears. Which also make two kinds of servants. For there is a servant who is also a son, who fears the Lord and honours the father, whence Malachi: *If I am Lord, where is my fear? If father, where is my honour? ((Malach. I))*. And there is a servant who fears punishment, but does not love justice. And because mention is made of fears, it is to be known that besides the natural fear, which is in all, there are four fears, namely: the worldly, which is evil and not from God; and the servile, which is good and from God, but is not sufficient; the initial, which is good and sufficient; and the chaste, which is good and perfecting, of which it is here treated: *For it begets us sons of God. In whom we cry.* This again is from the gift of the Spirit, which makes us so to cry *Abba,* in Hebrew, *father* in Latin. *Abba, father.* Because of the mystery, the Apostle set down both. And in his passion Christ said, *Abba, father,* because the Church is of both peoples, and suffering with her he showed in himself that her sons (the martyrs, namely) ought not to despair, if at the time of passion any sadness from human frailty should creep in.

*That we are the sons of God.* This the Holy Spirit makes us to recognize, while in the Church remission of sins is made; which although the whole Trinity works, yet it is understood to pertain to the Holy Spirit, because he is common to the Father and the Son, and the union of both; through whom is made that fellowship and unity by which we are made one body of the only-begotten Son of God. For unity joins us together, which charity makes, which is not save from the Holy Spirit. These things are said that we may love unity, and fear separation.

*Heirs.* Even though God does not depart, which is spoken according to human laws. Or he will depart, so that he be not seen through a glass in a dark manner as now, but face to face. It can also be said that Christ our head, departing to the passion, left us the possession of ecclesiastical peace, as he himself says: *My peace I give to you, my peace I leave to you ((Joan. XIV))*. Christ also is our inheritance. Whence: *The Lord is the portion of my inheritance ((Psal. XV))*, etc.

*If yet we suffer with him.* To mortify the deeds of the flesh, whence life shall be, no one can without trouble, for which patience is necessary.

notes.text: A ruler — One of the great council.
The same came — Through desire; but by night - Through shame: We know - Even we rulers and Pharisees.

Jesus answered — That knowledge will not avail thee unless thou be born again - Otherwise thou canst not see, that is, experience and enjoy, either the inward or the glorious kingdom of God. In this solemn discourse our Lord shows, that no external profession, no ceremonial ordinances or privileges of birth, could entitle any to the blessings of the Messiah's kingdom: that an entire change of heart as well as of life was necessary for that purpose: that this could only be wrought in man by the almighty power of God: that every man born into the world was by nature in a state of sin, condemnation, and misery: that the free mercy of God had given his Son to deliver them from it, and to raise them to a blessed immortality: that all mankind, Gentiles as well as Jews, might share in these benefits, procured by his being lifted up on the cross, and to be received by faith in him: but that if they rejected him, their eternal, aggravated condemnation, would be the certain consequence. Except a man be born again - If our Lord by being born again means only reformation of life, instead of making any new discovery, he has only thrown a great deal of obscurity on what was before plain and obvious.
When he is old — As Nicodemus himself was.
Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit — Except he experience that great inward change by the Spirit, and be baptized (wherever baptism can be had) as the outward sign and means of it.
That which is born of the flesh is flesh — Mere flesh, void of the Spirit, yea, at enmity with it; And that which is born of the Spirit is spirit - Is spiritual, heavenly, divine, like its Author.

Ye must be born again — To be born again, is to be inwardly changed from all sinfulness to all holiness. It is fitly so called, because as great a change then passes on the soul as passes on the body when it is born into the world.

The wind bloweth — According to its own nature, not thy will, and thou hearest the sound thereof - Thou art sure it doth blow, but canst not explain the particular manner of its acting. So is every one that is born of the Spirit - The fact is plain, the manner of his operations inexplicable.
We speak what we know — I and all that believe in me.

Earthly things — Things done on earth; such as the new birth, and the present privileges of the children of God. Heavenly things - Such as the eternity of the Son, and the unity of the Father, Son, and Spirit.

For no one — For here you must rely on my single testimony, whereas there you have a cloud of witnesses: Hath gone up to heaven, but he that came down from heaven. Who is in heaven - Therefore he is omnipresent; else he could not be in heaven and on earth at once. This is a plain instance of what is usually termed the communication of properties between the Divine and human nature; whereby what is proper to the Divine nature is spoken concerning the human, and what is proper to the human is, as here, spoken of the Divine.
And as Moses — And even this single witness will soon be taken from you; yea, and in a most ignominious manner. Num. xxi, 8, 9.

That whosoever — He must be lifted up, that hereby he may purchase salvation for all believers: all those who look to him by faith recover spiritual health, even as all that looked at that serpent recovered bodily health.

Yea, and this was the very design of God's love in sending him into the world. Whosoever believeth on him — With that faith which worketh by love, and hold fast the beginning of his confidence steadfast to the end. God so loved the world - That is, all men under heaven; even those that despise his love, and will for that cause finally perish. Otherwise not to believe would be no sin to them. For what should they believe? Ought they to believe that Christ was given for them? Then he was given for them. He gave his only Son - Truly and seriously. And the Son of God gave himself, Gal. iv, 4, truly and seriously.
God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world — Although many accuse him of it.

glossa.text: *And there was a man,* etc. This man was one of those who had believed through the signs. *Nicodemus by name.* Nicodemus, the victory of the people, or the victor of the people, bearing the figure of all those who, from the Jewish people believing in Christ, overcome the world through faith.

*He came,* etc. Night signifies the letter of the law, or the ignorance of the heart, or fear. And perhaps he came by night because, as a master in Israel, he would blush to speak openly, or from dread of the Jews. Because he had prudently noted the manifest signs, he asks more fully after the mysteries of faith; and therefore he deserved to be taught concerning the deity of Christ and his twofold nativity, concerning the passion, the resurrection and the ascension, concerning the second generation and the entry into the kingdom of heaven, and concerning many other things.

*Amen, amen I say.* To one who does not ask he expounds the second nativity, lest Nicodemus should believe that faith alone, on account of which, the signs being seen, he had believed in Jesus, suffices for salvation without the power of spiritual regeneration and without the sacraments. Also, because Nicodemus understood him to be a mere man, like John the Baptist or any one of the prophets, therefore Jesus began to instruct him concerning the second regeneration, by which he understands him to be the Son of God, and himself able to be made a son of God.

((AUG.)) The second nativity of which Jesus teaches is spiritual, which is of God and the Church unto life; but that man is minded only of the carnal, which is of Adam and Eve unto death. But as he says that the carnal cannot be repeated, so neither can the spiritual, by whomsoever it is performed, be repeated. For they are born of the seed of the true Abraham, whether through the free woman or through the handmaid.

*Unless a man.* The visible sacrament of water is necessary for the washing of the visible body, as the doctrine of invisible faith is necessary also for the sanctification of the invisible soul.

*Shall have been born again. ((CHRYS.))* That is, if thou hast not been born from above, and hast not received the certainty of the doctrines, thou wanderest somewhere outside and art far from the kingdom of heaven; showing and pointing to himself here, since it is not only this that is seen, but there is need of other eyes for the seeing of God.

*Of water.* Of water, the visible sacrament, and of the Spirit, the invisible understanding: so that a man may visibly receive the symbol of baptism, and may bring to completion the spiritual understanding of that same symbol. Or: of visible water and of the Holy Spirit.

*That which is born.* He distinguishes this spiritual nativity from the carnal, saying: *That which is born. Of the flesh.* That is, that which is from the first man by the succession of the flesh is carnal. By the name of flesh he signifies not only the flesh, but the whole carnal man. So, on the contrary, the whole spiritual man, in soul and body, is called spirit. *And that which,* etc. By the word and by the sacrament the Spirit is invisibly present, whereby he who is born of Adam unto death is born a son of God unto life: who is called not only spiritual, but spirit, because, as the substance of a spirit is invisible, so invisibly, through the visible sacrament, he is made a son of God. *Is spirit.* But do not wonder if I so call what is born spirit, because, as the spirit breathes where it will, and thou knowest not whence it comes or whither it goes, so is everyone that is born of the Spirit.

*The Spirit where he will.* By which he has in his power whose heart he shall enlighten. Thou hearest his voice in the Scriptures, or when someone full of the Holy Spirit speaks; and even if thou hearest it, thou knowest not whence it comes, that is, how it entered that man's heart, or how it returned, because its nature is invisible. So is everyone that is born of the Holy Spirit, because, by the invisible working of the Spirit, he begins to be what he was not, so that the unbeliever knows not whence he comes and whither he goes, that is, by what grace he comes into the adoption of a son, and goes into the kingdom of God. And because these things are unknown to the carnal man, he asks again? How can these things be done, not having the spiritual understanding within the letter of the law; he thinks impossible what is said of the nativity through the Spirit, whence he is reproved by the Lord: *Thou art a master,* etc. *And his voice,* etc. The voice of the Spirit is the voice of Christ, which Nicodemus heard; but because he is not yet born of the Spirit, he knows not whence it comes or whither it goes, that is, by what occasion he wills a man to be born in the Spirit, or whither it goes, that is, to what perfection he says that man is born of him. For he who is born of him is made one spirit with him by grace, as he himself also is one spirit by nature.

*Thou art a master,* etc. He does not insult him, so that he who is set over all should be held superior to him; but because he wills him to be born of the Spirit, which he cannot be unless he is humble, he humbles one swollen with his mastership. As if he should say: Proud prince, thou knowest nothing; humble thyself as did he who emptied himself, and, born of the Spirit, thou shalt know what now thou knowest not.

*We speak what we know.* That is, because he himself is the knowledge, the speech and the word of the Father. *And what we have seen we testify.* Because he himself is the vision, and the true testimony and truth of the Father. Which, being in the plural, intimates the mystery of the Trinity.

*If I have spoken to you earthly things. ((AUG.))* And because you do not receive earthly things, how can you take in the heavenly, that is, the heavenly nativity of the Spirit? since you not only do not believe, but do not even understand earthly things, namely what I said of the temple of my body (which I took from the earth), to be destroyed by you, to be raised up by me.

*But he that descended.* This pertains to the second nativity in the Spirit, because no one ascends in Christ to the Father but he who is born of the Spirit. No one is saved through the death of Christ but he who is born of the Spirit. No one is born of the Spirit but in the death of Christ. And when he says the Son of man, he gives us the assurance of ascending, since we are sons of men.

*And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the desert.* He puts forward his own death, which is the origin and the cause of having the things aforesaid, and in faith of it he instructs him. And because he was carnal, and versed in the law, therefore he brings forward a certain part of the law, which he shows to be a figure and significative of his own death, so that in this way it may be plain of the other parts of the law also that they are in figure. And because death is understood by the serpent, and Christ dead is called a serpent, whom he who beholds with faith is set free; as by the beholding of that other one in the figure they are set free from the fiery serpents, which signify the incitements of the vices. *So must the Son of man be lifted up,* etc. He invites the master of the law to the signification of the law. And because he had spoken of the Son of man, lest Nicodemus should think this only, he subjoins that the same is also the Son of God. *For God so loved.* He opens the cause of human salvation, namely, the love of God the Father, from whom all restoration is through his Son in the Holy Spirit.

*The world.* Cosmos in Greek, which in Latin is rendered *mundus*, is called adornment. By the world, therefore, human nature is signified, not because according to the body it consists of the four elements, but because according to the soul it has been adorned by God and made to the image of God; wherefore God loves it to this end, that he may make it eternal.

*That he would give his only-begotten Son, that everyone who believes,* etc. Behold, he says the same of the Son of God which he said above of the Son of man, so that by him through whom we were founded in the deity, through the same we may be restored in the man.

echoes.text: You shall tell Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, Israel is my son, my firstborn, and I have said to you, “Let my son go, that he may serve me”; and you have refused to let him go. Behold, I will kill your son, your firstborn.’”
echoes.note: 'Israel is my son, my firstborn' grounds the sonship/adoption language of vv.14-17; the Spirit constitutes believers as 'children of God,' transferring Israel's sonship status to those led by the Spirit.

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people:
echoes.note: The Spirit enabling 'the ordinance of the law' to be 'fulfilled in us' (v.4) draws on the new-covenant promise to write the Torah on the heart, internalizing the law by divine agency rather than external command.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit within you and cause you to walk in my statutes' undergirds vv.4-9: the indwelling Spirit (vv.9,11) produces obedience and 'walking according to the Spirit'; the verbal cluster Spirit-indwelling-walking-statutes is distinctive to Ezekiel.

echoes.text: I will put my Spirit in you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land: and you shall know that I, Yahweh, have spoken it and performed it, says Yahweh.
echoes.note: 'I will put my Spirit in you and you shall live' (the dry-bones vision) lies behind v.11, where the Spirit who raised Jesus 'will also give life to your mortal bodies'; Spirit-giving-life-to-dead-bodies is the precise Ezekielian figure.

echoes.text: Behold, I have set before you this day life and prosperity, and death and evil. For I command you this day to love Yahweh your God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments, his statutes, and his ordinances, that you may live and multiply, and that Yahweh your God may bless you in the land where you go in to possess it. But if your heart turns away, and you will not hear, but are drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce to […]
echoes.note: 'The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace' and 'if you live after the flesh you must die... by the Spirit... you will live' (vv.6,13) reframe the covenantal life-and-death choice of Moses' exhortation set before Israel.

echoes.text: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.
echoes.note: 'When Israel was a child I loved him, and out of Egypt I called my son' supplies the adopted-son-led-by-God motif (vv.14-15); the tender father-son relation undergirds the cry 'Abba! Father!'

echoes.text: Yet the number of the children of Israel will be as the sand of the sea, which can’t be measured nor numbered; and it will come to pass that, in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ they will be called ‘sons of the living God.’
echoes.note: 'In the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, it shall be said, You are children of the living God' anticipates 'these are children of God' / 'we are children of God' (vv.14,16); Paul cites this very text in Romans 9:26.

echoes.text: if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bull without defect to Yahweh for a sin offering.
echoes.note: 'for sin' (peri hamartias) in v.3 reproduces the Septuagint's standing phrase for the sin offering; God's sending his Son 'for sin' figurally casts Christ in the role of the Levitical purification sacrifice that 'condemns sin in the flesh.'

echoes.text: Yahweh said, “My Spirit will not strive with man forever, because he also is flesh; so his days will be one hundred twenty years.”
echoes.note: The flesh/Spirit antithesis (vv.5-9), where 'flesh' marks mortal humanity opposed to God's enduring Spirit, faintly recalls 'My Spirit will not abide in man forever, for he is flesh.'

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: 'The spirit is alive' / God giving 'life to your mortal bodies' (vv.10-11) faintly evokes the breath of life animating dust-formed Adam, now reapplied as resurrection-life by the Spirit.

echoes.text: For you are our Father, though Abraham doesn’t know us, and Israel does not acknowledge us: you, Yahweh, are our Father; our Redeemer from everlasting is your name.
echoes.note: 'You, O LORD, are our Father' — Israel's corporate address of God as Father — stands behind the Spirit-prompted filial cry 'Abba! Father!' (v.15).

echoes.text: “But I said, ‘How I would put you among the children, and give you a pleasant land, a goodly heritage of the armies of the nations!’ and I said, ‘You shall call me “My Father”, and shall not turn away from following me.’
echoes.note: 'I thought you would call me My Father and would not turn from following me' — God's hope that adopted Israel address him as Father — resonates with the adoptive cry of v.15.

echoes.text: I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you will be my people.
echoes.note: The covenant formula 'I will... be your God, and you shall be my people,' realized through the indwelling Spirit (vv.9-16), faintly underlies the divine-belonging and sonship affirmed by the Spirit's testimony.

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: Being 'born of water and spirit' fuses the two halves of Ezekiel's new-covenant oracle: God sprinkles 'clean water' for cleansing and puts a 'new spirit' within. The water-then-spirit sequence and the regeneration theme give high volume and coherence; Jesus' rebuke that 'the teacher of Israel' should know this presumes a known prophetic text.

echoes.text: Then he said to me, Prophesy to the wind, prophesy, son of man, and tell the wind, Thus says the Lord Yahweh: Come from the four winds, breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them, and they lived, and stood up on their feet, an exceedingly great army. Then he said to me, Son of man, these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried up, and our hope […]
echoes.note: The wind that 'blows where it wants to' and the one 'born of the Spirit' echo Ezekiel's valley vision where the ruach/breath comes from the four winds to give life. The Hebrew ruach pun (wind/spirit/breath) underlies both Ezek 37 and John 3:8; high coherence with the new-creation/resurrection motif of new birth.

echoes.text: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says Yahweh: I will put my law in their inward parts, and in their heart will I write it; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people:
echoes.note: The new-covenant promise of an inward, Spirit-written law ('I will put my law within them') coheres with regeneration 'from above.' Recurrence of new-covenant texts (alongside Ezek 36-37) strengthens the cluster, though John makes no verbal quotation.

echoes.text: As you don’t know what is the way of the wind, nor how the bones grow in the womb of her who is with child; even so you don’t know the work of God who does all.
echoes.note: 'As you do not know the way of the wind (ruach)... so you do not know the work of God' supplies the exact analogy of 3:8: the unknowable course of the wind/spirit mirrors the mystery of divine begetting in the womb. High coherence and a shared sapiential ruach-pun; verbal volume is moderate.

echoes.text: “For the unclean, they shall take of the ashes of the burning of the sin offering; and running water shall be poured into a vessel. A clean person shall take hyssop, dip it in the water, and sprinkle it on the tent, on all the vessels, on the persons who were there, and on him who touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead, or the grave. The clean person shall sprinkle on the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day. On the seventh day, he shall […]
echoes.note: The 'water of cleansing' / sprinkling rite for purification may stand behind 'born of water,' especially given v.25's dispute 'about purification.' Faint and contested; the water imagery is more naturally Ezekiel's, but the purification context raises availability.

echoes.text: He lays the beams of his rooms in the waters. He makes the clouds his chariot. He walks on the wings of the wind. He makes his messengers winds; his servants flames of fire.
echoes.note: The Psalm makes winds God's messengers and 'when you send forth your Spirit (ruach), they are created.' Resonates with wind/Spirit/new-creation in 3:5-8 but is faint and diffuse.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: The Spirit/wind (ruach) hovering at creation undergirds 'born of the Spirit' as new creation; coheres with John's creation framing (1:1-3) but verbal contact with ch.3 is faint.

echoes.text: Yahweh God formed man from the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.
echoes.note: God breathing the breath of life to make the man a living being stands behind Spirit-begetting as the giving of new life; low volume, drawn in by the ruach/breath cluster of 3:6-8.

echoes.text: Who has ascended up into heaven, and descended? Who has gathered the wind in his fists? Who has bound the waters in his garment? Who has established all the ends of the earth? What is his name, and what is his son’s name, if you know?
echoes.note: 'Who has ascended to heaven and come down? ... What is his name, and his son's name?' is strikingly answered by 3:13 ('No one has ascended... but he who descended, the Son of Man'). High volume of shared ascent/descent language plus the 'son' motif; a recognized wisdom backdrop.

echoes.text: It is not in heaven, that you should say, “Who will go up for us to heaven, and bring it to us, and proclaim it to us, that we may do it?”
echoes.note: 'Who will ascend to heaven for us to bring it down?' frames revelation as something no human can fetch from heaven; 3:13 inverts this — the Son of Man alone has descended bearing heavenly things. Coherent revelation-from-above theme; moderate verbal contact.

echoes.text: I saw in the night visions, and behold, there came with the clouds of the sky one like a son of man, and he came even to the ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.
echoes.note: 'Son of Man' coming with the clouds of heaven supplies the title and the heaven-earth movement that John reworks as descent/ascent. Recurrent Johannine Son-of-Man usage gives coherence, though here the motion is reversed.

echoes.text: And hardly do we divine the things that are on earth, And the things that are close at hand we find with labor; But the things that are in the heavens who ever yet traced out? And who ever gained knowledge of your counsel, except you gave wisdom, And sent your holy spirit from on high?
echoes.note: 'We can hardly guess at what is on earth... but who has traced out what is in the heavens? Who has learned your counsel unless you have given wisdom and sent your holy spirit?' closely parallels 3:12's earthly-vs-heavenly things and the Spirit-given knowledge of 3:8-11. Strong conceptual coherence (Second-Temple availability).

echoes.text: The ox knows his owner, and the donkey his master’s crib; but Israel doesn’t know, my people don’t consider.”
echoes.note: 'Israel does not know, my people do not understand' may color Jesus' rebuke of 'the teacher of Israel' who does not understand (3:10). Faint thematic echo of Israel's failure to perceive.

echoes.text: I have not learned wisdom, neither do I have the knowledge of the Holy One.
echoes.note: 'I have not learned wisdom, nor have I knowledge of the Holy One' immediately precedes the ascent question and reinforces the human inability to grasp heavenly things (3:12); faint, drawn in with v.4.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Make a fiery serpent, and set it on a pole. It shall happen, that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.” Moses made a serpent of brass, and set it on the pole. If a serpent had bitten any man, when he looked at the serpent of brass, he lived.
echoes.note: The explicit typological centerpiece: 'As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up.' Direct verbal and figural correspondence — the lifted bronze serpent that the snake-bitten looked to and lived prefigures the crucified Son giving eternal life to those who believe. Maximal volume and coherence.

echoes.text: For even when terrible raging of wild beasts came upon your people, And they were perishing by the bites of crooked serpents, Your wrath continued not to the uttermost; But for admonition were they troubled for a short space, Having a token of salvation, To put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law: For he that turned toward it was not saved because of that which was seen, But because of you, the Saviour of all.
echoes.note: The Wisdom midrash on Numbers 21 clarifies that 'the one who turned toward it was saved, not by what was seen, but by you, the Savior of all' — exactly John's point that the serpent saves by directing faith beyond itself to God. Strong Second-Temple interpretive parallel, high coherence with 3:15's believing-and-living.

echoes.text: Behold, my servant shall deal wisely, he shall be exalted and lifted up, and shall be very high.
echoes.note: The Servant who is 'lifted up (hypsothesetai) and exalted' supplies the double sense of John's hypsoo (crucified/exalted) Son of Man. LXX verbal contact with the lifting-up vocabulary that John deploys here and in 8:28; 12:32-34.

echoes.text: He removed the high places, and broke the pillars, and cut down the Asherah: and he broke in pieces the bronze serpent that Moses had made; for in those days the children of Israel burned incense to it; and he called it Nehushtan.
echoes.note: Hezekiah's destruction of the bronze serpent (Nehushtan) is part of the object's canonical afterlife and may inform the careful 'not the bronze itself but faith' nuance; faint, supplementary to Num 21.

echoes.text: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, whom you love, even Isaac, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there for a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”
echoes.note: 'God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son' echoes the Aqedah where God says of Isaac 'your son, your only son, whom you love' and credits Abraham who 'did not withhold' him. The LXX agapetos / monogenes-equivalent and the giving of the beloved only son give strong figural volume and coherence.

echoes.text: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory is risen on you. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the peoples; but Yahweh will arise on you, and his glory shall be seen on you. Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your rising.
echoes.note: 'The light has come into the world' and nations coming to the light coheres with Isaiah's 'Arise, shine, for your light has come.' Recurrent Johannine light-coming-into-the-world motif (cf. 1:9; 8:12); moderate verbal contact.

echoes.text: “These are of those who rebel against the light. They don’t know its ways, nor stay in its paths. The murderer rises with the light. He kills the poor and needy. In the night he is like a thief. The eye also of the adulterer waits for the twilight, saying, ‘No eye shall see me.’ He disguises his face. In the dark they dig through houses. They shut themselves up in the daytime. They don’t know the light. For the morning is to all of them like thick […]
echoes.note: The evildoers who 'rebel against the light,' who do their deeds in darkness and for whom 'morning is like deep darkness,' closely parallel 3:19-20: those who do evil hate the light lest their works be exposed. Strong thematic coherence of light/darkness moral exposure.

echoes.text: The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light. Those who lived in the land of the shadow of death, on them the light has shined.
echoes.note: 'The people who walked in darkness have seen a great light' supplies the light-into-darkness frame of 3:19; faint, part of the broader Isaianic light cluster.

echoes.text: For whoever finds me, finds life, and will obtain favor from Yahweh. But he who sins against me wrongs his own soul. All those who hate me love death.”
echoes.note: 'Whoever finds me finds life... all who hate me love death' parallels the believe-and-live / hate-the-light-love-darkness antithesis of 3:16-20 in a wisdom register; faint.

echoes.text: But for admonition were they troubled for a short space, Having a token of salvation, To put them in remembrance of the commandment of your law: For he that turned toward it was not saved because of that which was seen, But because of you, the Saviour of all.
echoes.note: The salvific 'looking' that brings life carries over from 3:14-15 into the believing-for-eternal-life of 3:15-16; low independent volume here, recurrence within the pericope cluster.

echoes.text: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.
echoes.note: 'Their works were evil' (3:19) faintly recalls the flood-judgment verdict that human deeds were continually evil; low volume, judgment register.

registers.label: Spare
lines: The voice of the Lord thunders over the waters.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
High above us a throne, and smoke, and a coal of fire.
Whom shall God send? Here we are.
The Spirit blows where it will, and we hear the sound.
By the Spirit we cry out, Abba, Father.
Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, come, let us worship.
We come to the God who is Three in One. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Listen — over the deep waters a voice is rolling like thunder, and the whole temple fills with smoke.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
Feel the wind move through the room; you cannot see where it comes from or where it goes, but it is the breath of God on your face.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
You were born of water and Spirit, and the same Spirit teaches your mouth one trembling word: Abba, Father.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord.
So come, you who are afraid and undone; the God of fire has touched your lips and called your name.
Holy, holy, holy is the Lord. Here we are; send us.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: The wind moves where it will; the Spirit is loose among us.
Holy is the Lord.
A coal of fire, a throne, a cry that shakes the door.
Holy is the Lord.
Born of water and the Spirit, we learn to say: Abba.
Holy is the Lord.
Come, let us worship Father, Son, and Spirit.
Holy is the Lord. Here we are; send us.
